title: Back to Hatchet and Sergeant Hatchet; Roosevelt Sykes in 1931
summary: Slim identifies Hatchet, his nicknames, his limited style and his link to Roosevelt Sykes in 1931.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I don't know. We'd go around and they found the box here. Did you know a piano player named Johnny Hodge in Memphis?

No. Hatchet, I didn't call anything. Hatchet, I know him. Hatchet, his first name? Yeah, Hatchet, me and him. I got him jobs as men in Arkansas for white people. I show Hatchet. They used to call him the Axe. Hatchet's a hot, deep slug. Something like, some big, like Himes in there. And, boom, them hard tents, you know.
Yeah. What was his first name, Hatchet?

Ah, I don't know his name. Willie Hatchet Wood. I don't know Hatchet's really his name. We call him Axe and we call him Hatchet, old fat, brown-skinned Hatchet. He used to play at Fulton Bill, Midway.
There was a Hatchet... Sergeant Hatchet.
Yeah, well... Yeah, well... You know, he quit playing piano after he come there from Memphis.
Oh, yeah. Well, he used to come on 7 or 8. Yeah, he'd come down there, but he didn't.
He didn't play? He played, so I tried to play. Because see, the music he played didn't fit the 7 or 8 club.

See, the thing about you, if you put you up there, you'd play with Robert Jr., Jim Tucker, anybody else, you see. See, and what they was playing, that's like a Hatchet called playing with Memphis Mini. He would sound like a fool playing with Memphis Mini, you understand what I mean? Because he was way over that kind of music.
Yes, yes. I understand. There was...
The other way, the man couldn't play as good as a brother in my book, but he used to have the name down there in a small era.

You understand? Yes, yes. But your Hatchet wasn't Sergeant Hatchet. Sergeant Hatchet is a different one. That's the same Hatchet. He went to work with these carnivales, Coin Man, like with these coin things. Sergeant and his other nickname was Bald Head, or what did you say? That's the same Hatchet. That's his nickname.
Didn't he have a brother or something?
I don't know about his brother, but the last time I seen him, he was at the county here at the Pirates. He stayed at the doctor there.

He did. Me and him been knowing. You understand the reason I know him? In 1931, I know him. Because when I got Roosevelt Sykes in 1931, Hatchet was the first to have 31 children. I come over there and got Roosevelt Sykes and brought him to Knight Street to Hunter's Place.
